name: Hyakinthia
summary: Three days at Amyclae that turn from mourning to song: offerings passed to Hyacinthus through the bronze door of his tomb beneath Apollo's throne, then the god's own day of choirs and riders.
testimonia: Pausanias 3.19.3–5 (the throne of Amyclae and Hyacinthus' tomb beneath it)
Athenaeus 4.139d–f (the three days, grief then festival)
Xenophon, Hellenica 4.5.11 (the Amyclaeans always go home for the Hyakinthia)
Spartan month Hyakinthios ≈ early summer — the Attic mapping is a convention
